verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents its own official MCP server, including a hosted version, that lets users manage flags, AgentControl configs, and observability data with natural language. Natural-language operation only works through a third-party MCP-capable AI client such as Cursor or Claude Code, and it covers a documented subset of resources rather than the whole product. missing for 10: a native in-product natural-language interface that needs no external AI client, documented coverage of all product operations by natural language, and independent or hands-on corroboration that natural-language commands work reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: you enable the server, then use it to manage flags, AgentControl configs, and observability data with natural language.
Configure the hosted MCP server so you can manage feature flags and AgentControl configs, and view observability data, directly from your AI client.
you must have an AI client that supports MCP, such as Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code with Copilot, or Windsurf.
